rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: # Biotechnological applications in medicine: insulin, gene therapy, therapeutic proteins ## 1. Introduction Opening frame for **Biotechnological applications in medicine** — what the topic is, why it matters, a real-world hook (Nepal where possible), the map of what follows, and the learning outcomes (biology-plan.md §3.1, block I). Prose depth is written in the Biotechnology and Its Applications fill pass. ## 2.…  ·  Medical biotech manufactures what the body fails to make, or fixes the gene itself. **Recombinant insulin** (1982) replaced animal pancreas extract. **Gene therapy** attempts to deliver a working gene into a patient's cells — the classic case being ADA-SCID ('bubble boy' immune deficiency), treated with the ADA gene delivered in a disabled vector.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: Human insulin: two-chain A (21 aa) + B (30 aa) linked by disulphide; proinsulin → C-peptide removed; engineered in E. coli since 1983 — the chain numbers are the marks.  ·  Trick 2: Gene therapy: ADA deficiency — lymphocytes from the patient, functional ADA gene inserted by retrovirus, cells returned (ex vivo); marrow transplant as alternative.

Key terms and statements Every new term defined once; exam-grade definitions live here and in keyPoints (block VI).  ·  **Worked example — why ADA-SCID was the right first case.** The disease is caused by ONE known gene; the target cells (bone marrow/lymphocytes) can be removed, treated outside the body and reinfused; and even partial ADA restoration gives clear clinical benefit.…  ·  ## 7. rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Most-asked points (NEB).** (1) Name three recombinant medical products. (2) Describe the ADA-SCID gene therapy procedure step by step. (3) Why is the therapy not heritable (somatic vs germline)? (4) What are the limitations of gene therapy? (5) How is the hepatitis B vaccine made by cloning?  ·  ## 8. Summary and self-check 5–10 line chapter summary, self-check questions and the common-confusions list (block VIII) — completed in the unit fill pass.  ·  **Summary.** Medicine runs on cloned genes at two levels: manufacture the missing protein (insulin, factor VIII) or deliver the missing gene (ADA-SCID). The first is routine; the second remains limited by vector safety and transience. **Self-check:** can you list the five steps of the ex vivo gene therapy protocol?
